title: Unramifiedness from ordinary fibres
statement: Let $h:Z\to B$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For every point $s\in B$, let $Z_s=Z\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre], where $\kappa(s)$ is the residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. If each $Z_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is a disjoint union of spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum] of finite separable algebraic field extensions [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] of $\kappa(s)$, then $h$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism].

mathlib_searches.query: a locally finite type morphism is unramified if every ordinary fibre is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable residue fields
mathlib_searches.results: Generic AlgebraicGeometry.FormallyUnramified and RingHom.FormallyUnramified APIs; no scheme-level fibre criterion.
No direct scheme-level ordinary-fibre criterion; only residue-field and formal-unramified declarations.

from.place: Proof (1)--(2), normal-cone specialization and the nearby-duality alteration reduction; Stacks nodal-family geometry: in the geometric-fibre unramifiedness criterion used for Sing(f)->S, the passage from ordinary fibres back to the morphism (Stacks Tag 02G8(2))
